name: Dafydd Stuttard
why_notable: Wrote the first version of Burp in 2003 under the long-standing hacking handle 'PortSwigger' ('one who swigs port'), originally to automate his own manual web-application testing, and founded PortSwigger Ltd (commonly dated 2008) to develop it into the industry-standard Burp Suite. He kept the company bootstrapped for roughly sixteen years before taking a first $112 million investment in 2024, retaining control. He co-authored The Web Application Hacker's Handbook (2007; 2nd ed. 2011) with Marcus Pinto — the canonical text on web testing — and created the core content of PortSwigger's free Web Security Academy, which trains millions and underpins the BSCP certification. Every penetration tester, bug-bounty hunter, red teamer and AppSec engineer who intercepts a request in Burp Proxy, replays it in Repeater or fuzzes it in Intruder is using the workflow he designed.
